title: Update PRD: translate cross-region failover postmortem actions into product requirements
creator: Arjun Patel
description:
Summary:
Following the February 28 cross-region failover incident (detailed in the postmortem), this ticket captures product-level requirement changes that translate engineering action items and reliability recommendations into a formal PRD update. Goal is to ensure future incidents of the same class (region outage causing degraded routing and long tail request failures) are mitigated through SLOs, observable guardrails, and rollout controls in the product surface (API/Console/Router).

Scope (what this PRD change will cover):
- New reliability requirements for cross-region failover behavior exposed to customers (expected failover latency, graceful fallback policy, retry/backoff guidance).
- Acceptance criteria for runtime SLOs, new health-check semantics, and canary routing policies.
- Operational requirements: dashboards, incident tracing retention, and automated alerting thresholds.
- UX/Console changes: rollout controls, visible fallback reason codes, and a per-customer failover log.
- Testing & QA: canary test plan, chaos test requirements, and e2e verification steps.

Out-of-scope for this PRD update: changes to billing model or dedicated capacity pricing; deep kernel/runtime kernel optimizations (these are tracked in ENG-2102).

Artifacts to link into updated PRD:
- Cross-region postmortem: https://confluence.company.com/display/RW/Cross-Region+Failover+Postmortem
- Incident timeline and traces: https://internal-logs.redwood.ai/incidents/2026-02-28-CRF
- Related engineering tickets: ENG-2102 (router fast-fail fallback), ENG-2098 (healthcheck granularity), ENG-2110 (tracing retention)
acceptance_criteria: PRD contains a clear customer-facing reliability SLA paragraph: 99th percentile cross-region failover latency <= 60s and documented fallback behavior
Console exposes per-route 'failover enabled' toggle and a human-readable rationale field for automatic fallbacks
Routing policy spec included: primary->secondary ordering, automatic cooldown (configurable), and maximum retry budget per request
Observability checklist included: dashboards for failover events, 99p/95p/median failover latency, and a dedicated log stream with failure reason codes
Automated tests described: canary scenario that simulates regional loss and validates automated routing within defined SLOs
E2E verification steps documented with pass/fail criteria and required test data sets
Design and security reviews scheduled and recorded with signoffs from Eng Lead and Security (links in PRD)
Dependencies to ENG tickets enumerated and gating criteria (ENG-2102 and ENG-2098 resolved or have agreed mitigations)
notes: PM/Eng working session 2026-03-03 produced revised SLO proposals and a split of UI vs runtime responsibilities. Need Design mockups for the Console toggle and failover reason UI by 2026-03-10.
